parts.style: warm, gentle morning welcome, speaking slowly
parts.text: Welcome, and good morning. <short pause> Today's devotional is The Good Shepherd... <short pause> a slow walk through the twenty-third Psalm. <short pause> You may know these words by heart. <short pause> Let's walk through them as if for the first time.

The psalm is David's, and David knew sheep. <short pause> Before he was a king, he was the youngest son, the one sent out to mind the flock. <short pause> He knew how easily sheep wander, and how much they need someone to look after them. <short pause> So when he looks for a picture of God, he chooses the work he knows... and he puts himself among the sheep.

The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want. He maketh me to lie down in green pastures: he leadeth me beside the still waters. He restoreth my soul: he leadeth me in the paths of righteousness for his name’s sake.

parts.style: slow, reflective, letting the words sink in
parts.text: The Lord is my shepherd. <short pause> Not only a shepherd. <short pause> My shepherd.

Look at who does the work in these lines. <short pause> He makes me lie down. <short pause> He leads. <short pause> He restores. <short pause> The sheep's part is to stay near and to follow. <short pause> Before you lead anything today... a meeting, a family, a classroom... you are first someone who is being led.
Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil: for thou art with me; thy rod and thy staff they comfort me.

Did you hear the change? <short pause> In the green pastures, David talks about God. <short pause> He leads me. <short pause> But in the valley, he begins to talk to God. <short pause> Thou art with me.

The good shepherd doesn't promise a road without valleys. <short pause> He promises His company on it. <short pause> He carries a rod to protect, and a staff to guide and to draw us back. <short pause> If today's path runs through a dark place, it does not mean you have lost the shepherd.

Thou preparest a table before me in the presence of mine enemies: thou anointest my head with oil; my cup runneth over. Surely goodness and mercy shall follow me all the days of my life: and I will dwell in the house of the Lord for ever. <long pause>

parts.style: gentle, a soft smile in the voice, illustrating
parts.text: The picture opens out, from a field to a table. <short pause> The sheep has become a guest. <short pause> The trouble is still in the room, and yet there is a meal, and a full cup. <short pause> And behind you, following all the way, come goodness and mercy.

So think about the day in front of you. <short pause> Where do you need to be led? <short pause> Where do you need company, more than answers? <short pause> You don't have to see the whole path this morning. <short pause> You only need to know whose voice you are following.

Let's pray. <short pause> Lord, my Shepherd, <short pause> go ahead of me today. <short pause> Slow me down where I am rushing, stay close where I am afraid, and bring me back when I wander. <short pause> Open my eyes to Your goodness along the way. <short pause> Amen.
Carry one line with you today... <short pause> the Lord is my shepherd. <short pause> When the day gets loud, come back to that one word, my. <short pause> Go in peace, and go well led.
